steps.message:
What is the actual key schedule in feal.c and decrypt.c, since the search you tried with expand((base+i)&0xFFFFF) came up empty. Is it really four consecutive 20 bit seeds, or are the four round keys obtained by some other transformation of the single seed. Have you printed the four round keys from either of the supplied programs for a test case.

In what numeric notation are the two 64 bit numbers written in pairs.txt, in particular whether they are hex or decimal and whether a leading minus sign is possible. The use of %lld in the trial program only works if that has been checked against the actual files. Are the numbers in ciphertexts.txt written in exactly the same way.

Which 32 bit half of a 64 bit number is the left half as far as the C code is concerned. Your last trial took the high 32 bits as the left half, but that may have been the whole of the difficulty. You need a single case which has been verified by running it through both of the supplied programs.

Have you yet determined the exact order in which the left and right halves are changed inside each of the four rounds. The final extra mixing step is very likely to have been put in the wrong place if it has not been checked line by line against the source.

What form of command line arguments do the two supplied programs take if you wish to run them with a set of keys that you have chosen yourself. The end of the job is impossible until you can do that for the numbers in ciphertexts.txt.

What notation must the final list of recovered numbers in plaintexts.txt use to be considered correct. That should of course be the same as that in which the unrecovered numbers are presented, but it has not been settled.
steps.reasoning_content:
We need to respond to user. They ask: "Please begin by asking several questions (at least five, more if necessary) about the current state of the solution that are not answered in the summary from the prior agent. After you ask these questions you will be on your own, so ask everything you need to know."

We need to output only questions? Probably yes. Need ask at least five questions about current state not answered. We have original task, summary, terminal screen. Need infer likely issues. We are picking up. We need know:
- Exact seed expansion used by actual feal.c/decrypt.c: are round keys expand(seed + i) with seed masked to 20 bits? Terminal seq.c assumed consecutive seeds and masked with &0xFFFFF. That failed. Maybe keys are expand(seed * something), or seed split? Need inspect source.
- Byte order for input numbers: are numbers in pairs.txt and ciphertexts.txt big-endian hex, decimal? Are they signed? They are read with %lld and split high/low 32 bits. Need know if file format has 16 hex digits or decimal.
- Which half is "left" and "right" in the C code: does it interpret top 32 bits as left? The trial maybe used a wrong convention. Need verify by a round-trip with known keys.
- The f_function and g_function parameters: does round use right^=left before round or after? Does the final output have an extra left ^= right? Need match actual source.
- The linear attack: which known relations exist in g_function, how many pairs needed, and how to handle multiple candidates. The previous agent only did a consecutive seed search. Need know if there are any partial results or candidate lists.
- What output format plaintexts.txt expects: same order as ciphertexts.txt, same numeric notation (hex/decimal, signed/unsigned, leading zeroes).
- Does decrypt.c expect the original 20 bit seed or the four expanded keys as command line arguments.
- Have any of the 32 pairs been used to test a candidate key and if so what was the outcome.

Need at least 5. Could ask 8. Ensure they are not answered in summary. Summary says both programs work together, only interpretation of numbers was difficulty, but doesn't answer these. It also says first of two numbers is input. But not enough. Need questions.

Need maybe mention that seq.c tried consecutive seeds. Ask if that was the only key schedule or if other schedules have been tried. Ask whether source files have been modified. Ask whether pairs.txt contains 32 full 64-bit pairs. Ask if ciphertexts.txt contains same notation. Ask if there are build scripts. We are on our own after. Good.

Need final in plain. No extra explanation.
